title: AUTHORED TEST: SYNTHESIZE-D2 join divisibility conditions with digit-order constraints
subject: TEST
scope_summary: Entirely original three-digit digit-choice task. Synthesize even-ending and digit-sum divisibility with largest-number ordering under distinct/fixed digits. Changed transfer examines which single swap preserves both checks and lowers a given multiple of six. No official source or KEY.

supports_claims: Hundreds fixed 4, digits drawn without repetition from 1..5: largest divisible-by-six three-digit integer is 432.
Single swap of distinct digits in 534, smaller and divisible-by-six, uniquely gives 354.
resources.selection_reason: Explicitly coordinate two familiar number tests and a positional-maximization constraint; learner owns candidate choice and verifies both tests, not a single divisibility procedure.

conventions.statement: For whole numbers, divisibility by six is equivalent to BOTH even last digit and digit sum divisible by three.
Digits must be used without repetition, and a three-digit number has a nonzero hundreds digit.
With hundreds fixed, maximize the tens digit first; an even final digit may constrain that choice.

capabilities.action: Synthesize the independent parity and digit-sum divisibility criteria with restricted available digits and place-value ordering to choose and verify one maximal candidate.
capabilities.success_criterion: With 4 fixed in hundreds and unused digits from {1,2,3,5}, identify 432 as the greatest divisible-by-six code and justify why 452 fails and no bigger valid code exists; in transfer analyze a downward one-swap transformation of 534.

microtopics.title: Combine parity, digit-sum and position choice when forming whole numbers
microtopics.badge_reason: Known checks connect to a new maximal candidate under fixed and distinct positions; the connection, not routine division, is learner-owned.
entry_assumptions: Read three-digit place value, compare hundreds/tens/ones.
An even number has an even final digit.
Use digit sum to test divisibility by three.
microtopics.inferential_jump: A candidate with the largest available tens digit can still FAIL the other divisibility criterion; revise the placement so BOTH independent checks and the ordering goal hold.

teaching_path.action: When making a multiple of six, separately check the LAST digit for evenness and the DIGIT SUM for being a multiple of three.
teaching_path.why_valid: 6=2×3 with coprime factors, so an integer divisible by both 2 and 3 is divisible by 6.
teaching_path.output: Two necessary and sufficient tests, used together

teaching_path.action: With hundreds digit 3 from 1,2,3,4, list the larger possible tens digits in descending order and choose a nonrepeated even final digit.
teaching_path.why_valid: A largest three-digit number prioritizes the tens digit after hundreds is fixed, but must also be even.
teaching_path.output: Test likely 34_ before 32_, then enforce final even

teaching_path.action: For candidate 342 check its last digit 2 (even) and digit sum 3+4+2=9, then compare any higher candidate.
teaching_path.why_valid: 342 passes both tests and higher 34_ with last digit 4 would repeat, so it cannot be improved.
teaching_path.output: 342 divisible by six and maximal in the worked digit set

teaching_path.action: Check 342÷6=57, and inspect 324 and 312 for why they are smaller while still eligible.
teaching_path.why_valid: Divisibility alone does not resolve the largest-valid-code comparison.
teaching_path.output: Worked candidate verified and order justified

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Any three-digit number ending in an even digit must be divisible by six.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Is 352 (even last digit) divisible by three? Add the digits before claiming divisible by six.
misconceptions.repair: Use the conjunction of two tests: even ones AND digit sum a multiple of three. 352 ends in two but 3+5+2=10, so it is not divisible by six.

exit_task.prompt: New unseen task: using three DISTINCT digits from {1,2,3,4,7}, with 7 fixed as the hundreds digit, construct the LARGEST three-digit multiple of six. Show how an even ending and digit sum jointly determine the choice; rule out any larger choice.

answer.summary: 732 is the greatest possible valid code.
reasoning: Hundreds is 7; choose the tens digit as high as possible with a different even last digit.
The candidate 742 is even but 7+4+2=13, so it fails divisibility by three. 734 is odd; 732 is even and has sum 12.
7 is fixed; the larger tens digit 4 has no valid distinct ones digit making multiple of six. 732 is therefore greatest.
answer.check: 7+3+2=12, 732÷6=122; any candidate above 732 with hundreds 7 would need tens 4 but fails either digit sum or even last digit.

predict.defensible_answer: The digit sum is 3+5+2=10, not divisible by 3, so 352 fails the second test.

boundary_test.prompt: Changed boundary: from digits {1,2,3,5,8}, make a three-digit number with 8 as hundreds and 5 FIXED as its last digit, using distinct digits. Can it be a multiple of six for ANY allowed tens digit? Test BOTH criteria after a written decision.
boundary_test.answer: No. Every such number ends in 5, so is odd and fails divisibility by 2; it cannot be divisible by 6 regardless of the tens digit or digit sum.
boundary_test.confirms: Both required conditions remain necessary; the odd fixed last digit is a decisive impossibility boundary.

relations.expression: For distinct allowed digits h,t,u and number N=100h+10t+u, N divisible by 6 exactly when u is even AND h+t+u is divisible by 3. With h fixed, compare t before u when finding the greatest valid N.
relations.meaning: The criterion conjunction and place-value ordering must all hold; a candidate satisfying one alone is insufficient.

question_families.title: Conjunction of digit divisibility and ordering under restricted permutations
solution_structure: Select valid distinct digit positions respecting a fixed hundreds digit.
Check last-digit evenness separately from divisibility of the digit sum by three.
Use place-value order to compare admissible candidates and rule out larger ones.
For changed transfer, track invariant digit sum under swaps while last-digit parity and order may change.

The tens digit 4 is highest available; with hundreds 3 and last digit 2, 342 has digit sum9 and even units, so passes both criteria.
Other candidates with tens below 4 are smaller than 342 regardless of eligibility.

questions.stem: Using any THREE DISTINCT digits chosen from {1,2,3,4,5}, form a three-digit number with 4 in the HUNDREDS place. It must be divisible by 6 and be the LARGEST possible number under these rules. Decide which digits to put in the TENS and ONES places, justify your choice by combining BOTH the even-last-digit rule AND the digit-sum divisibility-by-three rule, and show why no larger number works.
conditions: Tens and units come from {1,2,3,5} without repetitions.
Number must be divisible by both 2 and 3, equivalently by 6.
Wholly original authored TEST; no exam statement copied.
questions.failure_signal: Picks 452 because larger/even or picks 412/432 without digit-sum+maximality proof.

reasoning: Since 4 is fixed in hundreds and no repeats are allowed, the ONLY available even digit for ones is 2; hence all eligible numbers end in 2.
Choose tens 5 first to maximize: 452 is even but digit sum 4+5+2=11, not a multiple of three, so 452 fails.
Next highest tens is 3: 432 is even and has digit sum 4+3+2=9, a multiple of three, so 432 is divisible by six.
The only larger allowed tens choice was 5 and was rejected, so 432 is maximal. Lower tens1 would give412, which also fails sum.
answer.check: Compute 432÷6=72. The complete list of candidates ending2 with hundreds4 and distinct digits is {412,432,452}; only432 has digit sum divisible by3.

reasoning_route.action: Use 4 as hundreds; remaining positions must use distinct digits from the stated pool.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Digits cannot repeat and hundreds fixed means only 1,2,3,5 remain.

reasoning_route.action: Enforce both independent divisibility checks AND compare high tens candidates.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Only remaining even ones is 2. Tens 5 leads 452 (sum11 fail), tens3 leads 432 (sum9 pass).
reasoning_route.output: The conditions meet first at 432 in descending place order.

reasoning_route.action: Prove no larger choice remains and divide 432 by six.
reasoning_route.why_valid: If tens is lower than3, number is smaller; tens5 failed. The sum criterion and evenness are both necessary.

questions.stem: A safe three-digit code is 534, which is divisible by 6. You MUST swap EXACTLY TWO digit positions ONCE (no digit may be changed or added). The new three-digit code must be SMALLER than 534 while STILL divisible by 6. Analyze ALL three possible single position swaps. Which swap works, and why do the other two fail? Combine the invariant DIGIT-SUM check with the change in the LAST digit and numerical order.
conditions: Exactly one transposition (swap two of hundreds/tens/ones), not a replacement.
Result must remain a three-digit multiple of six and be strictly smaller than 534.
Wholly authored TEST, no source-exam provenance.

hints.text: What cannot change when you exchange two digit positions, and what might change about the LAST digit?

questions.failure_signal: Assumes any rearrangement of 534 stays divisible by six because digit sum is preserved, ignoring last digit.

answer.summary: Swap hundreds and tens: 354 is the only permissible result.
reasoning: Every one-swap candidate has the same three digits, so the digit sum remains5+3+4=12, divisible by three.
Swap hundreds and tens: 354 has last digit4 (even), and is smaller than534; 354÷6=59. All three requirements hold.
Swap hundreds and units: 435 has final digit5 (odd), so not divisible by two, even though435 is smaller and its sum remains12.
Swap tens and units: 543 ends in3 (odd), and it is larger than534; it fails both the parity and order checks.
The digit-sum invariant under rearrangement is not enough to preserve a multiple of six: the last-digit parity still matters.
answer.check: Three exact possibilities {354,435,543}; only354 is both even and <534. Independent division 354=6×59.

reasoning_route.action: List all distinct transpositions of 5,3,4 and preserve the digits.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Exactly one swap gives three results.

reasoning_route.action: Identify invariant digit sum under any swap, then test changed last-digit parity and numeric order.
reasoning_route.why_valid: Sum stays12, but only354 ends even and is less than534.

reasoning_route.action: Test each swap against all rules and divide successful number by six.

transfer.statement: Primary constructs the maximum legal multiple using a fixed hundreds digit and a digit pool; transfer begins with a valid complete number and requires exactly one position swap, then preservation of divisibility and strict decrease.
transfer.invariant: Rearrangements preserve the sum of digits, so the divisibility-by-three test stays fixed, while evenness and ordering depend on the final position.
